At a tuning that passes the RI-VIS04 bar strongly (radius 0.42, strength 1.9, no cap), this reads on real ground as a hard black-diamond checker matching the terrain's own triangulation, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. Mitigated, not solved: uAOMaxOcclusion (0.6) caps total darkening so the worst case is a visible grey-brown crease rather than solid black, and the wall/step contact itself still reads clearly darker (see production-thorn evidence). This softens the artifact considerably but does NOT remove it — it is still visible as a faint geometric grid on open ground in every production screenshot taken. The real fix is a smooth/interpolated normal (a G-buffer target, or reading a vertex-normal attribute already on the terrain mesh) and is out of scope for a compositor-only change; named as owed below. THIS IS THE HONEST HEADLINE OF THIS PIECE: the fix passes its acceptance bar and visibly improves contact grounding, and it also visibly textures open ground with an artifact that was not there before. Both are true and both are in the evidence pack.

owed_follow_on_terrain_facet_normal.what: Replace the depth-derivative normal in computeAO() with a real smooth normal: either add a normal render target (MRT alongside tWorld/tDepth) fed by an interpolated vertex normal already available on every mesh, or blur the AO term itself in a second pass rather than the single-pixel derivative used here.
owed_follow_on_terrain_facet_normal.why_not_done_here: Either route touches more than the compositor: an MRT normal target changes what every material's fragment shader outputs (bigger than the frozen MATERIAL_API's compositor seam), and a spatial blur of the AO term needs a second render target and pass this compositor does not have. Both are real work, not a one-line fix, and the acceptance bar this piece is judged against (RI-VIS04 §4 / RI-VIS03 M6b) does not require it.

summary: Replaced the existing fake 'AO' in the post-process composite (a depth-DISCONTINUITY detector that only darkens a hard silhouette edge, max 12%, and is blind to a continuous-depth contact like a step meeting a path) with a real ten-tap hemisphere screen-space AO in game/src/render/post/composite.js, reconstructed from the existing depth texture, with no new module-scope ShaderChunk patcher (self-contained ShaderMaterial — the shader-hook collision trap named in the dispatch does not apply to this seam, confirmed by gate).
why_this_seam_and_not_the_material_or_th: The sun DirectionalLight shadow map already exists (sky.js, PCFSoftShadowMap, tuned bias/normalBias/mapSize) and W1-30-SHADOW-CASTERS already landed broad caster/receiver flags across terrain, canopy, geology and buildings — so directional cast shadows are not the gap.

W1-ORPHANED-SURFACE-SHADERS (V1, landed same day) found and recorded the actual AO gap directly: worldMaterial() sets aoMap:null on every family with an authored set (all twenty), and 'there is no screen-space AO pass anywhere in game/src/render — only a comment in visual-foundation.js:676 deferring to W1-30A's GTAO stack, which does not exist in the tree.' That comment is stale: a compositeMaterial.uniforms.uAO already existed and was wired to a quality toggle, but what it DID was the weak edge detector described above, not ambient occlusion.

MATERIAL_API.md is frozen (§9: additions only). This fix does not touch worldMaterial(), the twenty families, or any option key — it is entirely inside the compositor, which is not part of the frozen surface.

the_fix.mechanism: Ten-tap hemisphere SSAO. viewPosFromDepth() reconstructs view-space position from the existing depth texture and the camera's projectionMatrixInverse (pushed every frame from renderer.js — the camera moves every frame). Normal is estimated from the position's own screen-space derivative (cross(dFdx(P),dFdy(P))), the standard technique when no G-buffer normal exists. Ten hardcoded, hemisphere-biased kernel samples (deterministic — no per-frame randomness, matching the existing dither pass's own determinism requirement) are rotated per-pixel by the same static interleaved-gradient-noise hash the dither already uses, offset from P, re-projected to screen space via the camera's forward projectionMatrix, and compared against the real depth there with a distance range check. uAO stays the on/off name and meaning every existing tool (tools/render/w1-30-*.mjs) already flips; what changed is what it does when on.
the_fix.final_shipped_uniforms: uProjMat, uInvProjMat (mat4, pushed every frame from renderer.js). uAORadius=0.42 (metres), uAOStrength=3.1, uAOBias=0.03 (metres), uAOMaxOcclusion=0.6 — the cap that trades some acceptance-bar margin for a much softer terrain artifact (see could_not_do). All additive to the existing uniform set, nothing removed or renamed.
the_fix.why_no_shader_hook_collision: This is a self-contained THREE.ShaderMaterial fragment shader already owned by render/post/composite.js since W1-30S/A. It does not touch THREE.ShaderChunk at module scope (the two known collision sites are game/src/world/aerial.js and game/src/render/sky.js, both fog) and does not touch actor.js/visual-foundation.js's onBeforeCompile chaining (the seam behind the character-body link failure above). tools/visual/w1-30-shader-hook-collision.mjs run before and after this change proves the FOG-CHUNKS-SINGLE-OWNER check is unaffected either way.

the_bug_found_and_fixed_while_building_t: The first working version of computeAO() sent the estimated view-space normal the WRONG way (testing N.z > 0.0), which points every hemisphere kernel sample INTO the surface instead of out over it. Measured effect: the ENTIRE FRAME went solid black end to end whenever uAO was on. Fixed by working out the view-space sign convention on paper (camera looks down -Z, a front-facing normal has positive Z) and flipping the condition to N.z < 0.0. Recorded here because RULES rule 4 asks that a probe capable of failing be shown failing, and this is that evidence for the shader itself, not just for the gate around it — and because a wrong-signed normal is exactly the kind of error a screenshot catches and a stats-only check would not: boot-check (engine constructs, answers ready()) passed the whole time this was broken, because it never renders and inspects a frame.

v2_vs_v3_judgement.question: Is V2 alone enough, or is V3 (ambient/GI fill, 3/5 judges) needed before a re-judgement is worth paying for?
v2_vs_v3_judgement.answer: V2 ALONE IS LIKELY NOT ENOUGH, AND V3 SHOULD LAND BEFORE THE NEXT RE-JUDGEMENT. Read plainly: R2 (this piece, 5/5 judges, the most universal single observation) is addressed — contact junctions now measurably darken, evidenced multiple ways. But the verdict's own reading (cluster analysis) makes clusters A/B/C 'three faces of one condition: surfaces in our build are not shaded, they are filled' — and R3's cluster (3/5 judges, 'shadowed regions crushed to a near-uniform black with no bounced or ambient fill') is a DIFFERENT axis (shadow-side ambient response, not contact geometry) that this piece does not touch at all. A judge shown a wave-2 pair would likely still find crushed, ambient-less shadows even with contact AO now present, because R2 and R3 are additive, not overlapping, defects. Spending a re-judgement before R3 risks the same shape of result as the R1/R2/R3 split in the original verdict: partial credit, not a reversal.
v2_vs_v3_judgement.what_would_overturn_it: A cheap check before committing to R3's cost: capture the same material_showcase junction (or a real production building) in the SHADOW side of the frame (sun behind the object) and read the shadow-region luma the way RI-VIS03 M6 does. If it already reads well above 'crushed' (i.e. R3's defect happens to already be mild in this build, contrary to the original verdict's reading), R3's priority drops and a re-judgement on V2 alone becomes more defensible. Not done here — it is a half-day instrument, not a five-minute one, and is the natural next dispatch.
